title: Contextual Generative Auction with Permutation-level Externalities for Online Advertising

problem.claim: Online ad auctions must account for interactions among displayed items rather than relying on independent click-through rates.

gap.claim: Existing learning-based auction methods use a prediction-before-allocation paradigm that fails to model externalities arising from the context of the final allocation.

contributions.claim: Introduces Contextual Generative Auction, a framework for modeling permutation-level externalities in multi-slot ad auctions.
Decouples allocation and payment optimization based on a theoretically derived optimal auction structure.
Uses an autoregressive allocation model and an ex-post-regret formulation of incentive compatibility to learn payment rules end to end.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CGA as a novel framework incorporating permutation-level externalities in multi-slot ad auctions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive offline and online experiments showing higher platform revenue and CTR than existing methods.
The authors report that CGA approximates the optimal auction with nearly maximal revenue and minimal regret.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online advertising revenue depends substantially on ad auctions.
Classical mechanisms fail to capture interactions among displayed items, while newer learning-based approaches encode context but retain a restrictive allocation paradigm.
CGA models permutation-level externalities and separates allocation optimization from payment optimization.
The framework uses autoregressive allocation generation and ex-post regret minimization to learn payments end to end.
The authors report improvements in revenue and CTR and close approximation to the optimal auction.

source_observation.claim: When outcomes depend on the jointly ordered set of selected items, modeling only candidate-set interactions may miss allocation-context effects.

interpretation.claim: The allocation itself should be part of the modeled context when externalities depend on permutations.

application.claim: Consider allocation models that represent ordered or permutation-level interactions in multi-slot recommendation or auction settings.

exception.claim: This lesson may not apply when item effects are adequately captured by independent or set-level assumptions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, experimental scale, baseline implementations, or numerical improvements.
The abstract does not provide the formal assumptions or proof details for the theoretically derived optimal auction.
The abstract does not describe the online deployment setting or duration of the online experiments.
